model.name: Prinz et al. 2003/2004 stomatogastric AB/PD pacemaker neuron (AB_PD_3 parameter set)
model.citation: Prinz AA, Billimoria CP, Marder E (2003). Alternative to Hand-Tuning Conductance-Based Models: Construction and Analysis of Databases of Model Neurons. Journal of Neurophysiology 90(6):3998-4015. doi:10.1152/jn.00641.2003 | Prinz AA, Bucher D, Marder E (2004). Similar network activity from disparate circuit parameters. Nature Neuroscience 7(12):1345-1352. doi:10.1038/nn1352
model.expected_behavior: Single compartment; Na, CaT, CaS, KA, KCa, Kd, H (Ih), Ca pool. Expected bursting pacemaker (AB/PD). Screening (jNeuroML, not calibrated, not eFEL; verification.json run 2026-09-13T16:00:56+00:00_aa8fa6a0): shipped harness gives 40 spikes in 5 s in 2 bursts on slow waves; spontaneously active. Hyperpolarisation with depolarising recovery in a spontaneously active cell: -0.3 nA for 1 s reaches -124.5 mV at +264 ms and recovers by 43.2 mV before release, then 13 rebound spikes. Sag ratio undefined (spikes in the pre-step baseline window). Ih contribution to that recovery untested: the Ih-block run of this protocol aborted in jLEMS. At -0.1 nA (spikes during the step with and without Ih) blocking Ih lowered the end-of-step potential by 12.3 mV.
model.inclusion_reason: Candidate for the bursting and rebound gaps (independent source, MIT, jnml-valid). Not shown to fill the Ih/sag gap: sag ratio is undefined in this spontaneously active cell and the Ih-block control of the recovering protocol aborted. Decisions needed: rheobase for spontaneously active cells (fallback 0.1 nA used), canonical window (earliest harness pulse is 0-100 ms), burst onsets 1.6 s apart vs 700-1000 ms protocols; harness is a network (AB_PD is presynaptic only).
